content: The primary objective of this technology is to treat pulmonary diseases using aerosolized perfluorocarbon (PFC). This innovative approach involves the aerosolization of PFC through an introducible jet-nebulizer device known as the Aer-Probe (developed by Trudell). The efficacy of this method has been demonstrated in multiple animal studies conducted by researchers such as Kandler and von der Hardt. The aerosolized delivery of PFC provides a safe and user-friendly method for implementing perfluorocarbon-assisted ventilation. Patients suffering from acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and neonatal respiratory distress syndrome have shown significant and sustained improvements in gas exchange and lung mechanics when treated with this technology. Additionally, the use of aerosolized PFC has been shown to mitigate ventilator-associated lung injury by reducing the inflammatory processes that contribute to chronic lung disease. This technology is versatile and can be applied to various perfluorocarbons, regardless of their molecular structure, offering the potential to develop and register specific PFCs as respiratory therapeutics. Recent studies have demonstrated that in neonatal piglets with surfactant depletion-induced lung injury (achieved through repeated saline lung lavage), the use of aerosolized PFC as a ventilatory strategy resulted in a reduction of the initial pulmonary inflammatory response and an improvement in gas exchange. Specifically, the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines such as IL-1ß, IL-6, IL-8, and TGF-ß1 in pulmonary tissue was significantly lower in piglets treated with aerosolized PFC compared to those ventilated with intermittent mandatory ventilation. These findings were reported by von der Hardt and Kandler. Furthermore, in the same surfactant-depleted piglet model, the mRNA expression of inflammation-related adhesion molecules, including E-Selectin, P-Selectin, and ICAM-1, was effectively reduced when aerosolized PFC was used. This was highlighted in studies by Schoof and von der Hardt. Treatment with aerosolized PFC also led to a significant reduction in neutrophil infiltration within lung tissue. The modulation of pro-inflammatory cytokines and intercellular adhesion molecules in porcine lung tissue, which are key contributors to acute pulmonary inflammatory responses, was achieved through this novel protective respiratory support strategy using aerosolized PFC.
